evidence_notes: Hypothesized prompt: evaluate how well the author supports the idea that studying Venus is a worthy pursuit despite the dangers. Claim = 'the author supports the idea that studying Venus is worthy pursuit despite the dangers'; the body is a walk through paragraphs 1-8 of the source, each introduced by 'in paragraph X it says' followed by a long verbatim quotation (roughly 60% of the essay's words are quoted); no quote is interpreted. org 3 (controlling idea is stated but rung 4 fails: no closing at all, essay stops on a quote, and the para-1/2 quotes about brightness and density do not bear on the claim). dev 2 (rung 3 fails as applied: the only specifics are borrowed and stand in for the argument entirely - the essay reports what the source says instead of arguing from it; not scored 1 because the writer's own frame and attribution tags survive). conv 2 (rung 3 fails: 'supports the idea that studying Venus is worthy pursuit despite the dangers by, in paragraph 3 and 4' and 'Which is by, out of all the other paragraphs, he is actually writing all the main ideas' force the reader to guess what was intended). arg 2 (rung 3 fails: the prompt's own wording handed back with no commitment added; 'he is actually writing all the main ideas' is the only appraisal offered).

Hypothesized prompt: evaluate how well the author supports the idea that studying Venus is worthy despite the dangers. Claim = exploring Venus is worth NASA's time because it could determine whether Venus is habitable. Support drawn from the source and paraphrased: no craft has landed in thirty years and most became worthless quickly; ~800 degrees, 97% CO2 atmosphere, sulfuric acid clouds, ninety times Earth's pressure; NASA's proposal to float a crew 30 miles above the surface. org 5 (rung 5: order is motivated - failures, then the conditions that caused them, then NASA's workarounds; no pair swaps without loss; rung 6 fails, the sequence's move is not sustained and the close only partly advances the opening). dev 4 (rung 5 fails: the paragraph of atmospheric conditions is a list of specifics left to speak for itself, so 'most explained' is not met; rung 4 met - 'Zero research was able to be done due to the extremes of the planet', 'Though he would be floating 30 miles up... we would gather more information'). conv 4 (rung 5 fails: 'setting us further in the future than never before' and 'shows the strive to gather information' wrong-foot the reader; rung 4 holds - MASA, plnaet, exlplains are visible but need no repair). arg 4 (rung 5 fails on (d): the conclusion - the author makes his case, Venus is worth pursuing - is what the prompt's framing already implies, and the answer to the dangers is reported from the source rather than argued; rung 4 met, habitability-for-survival is a reason with a stated why).

Prompt (source-based): is the Face on Mars a natural landform or alien-made? Claim = natural landform, stated in the intro with two announced reasons. Support: the Mars Global Surveyor image quoted from para 7 ('a natural landform. There was no alien monument after all'), the butte/mesa comparison and Garvin's Middle Butte quote from para 12, and the para 5 quote showing the alien reading originates with conspiracy theorists, not NASA. org 4 (rung 5 fails: the two body parts - photographic evidence, and the provenance of the alien claim - are announced as a list in the intro and could swap without loss; rung 4 met, idea stated early, frame present, all parts on topic). dev 4 (rung 5 fails: quotes are specific and marked but the explanation is restatement - 'That's a big piece of evidence that it's not made by aliens' - and the Garvin/mesa quote gets no interpretation; rung 4 met, the connection is stated for some support). conv 3 (rung 4 fails: 'those remakes are not all true they are just theories which is just provided by evience but, not always right' and 'Maybe, you people that think that it's made by aliens I hope my reasonings...' need repair on re-reading, and errors accumulate - evience, conspircy, theroists, you're for your). arg 4 (rung 5 fails on (d): the conclusion is one of the two options the prompt's framing already supplies; rung 4 met - the essay reasons that conspiracy claims are theories, not verified findings, and so should be weighed against expert sources).

Prompt (source-based): should driverless cars be developed? Claim = they would be a success and development is already in a positive position, though safety risks remain. Support: cars that brake, steer and accelerate themselves; all models notify the driver when the road requires human skill, plus windshield flashing lights, heads-up displays and GM's vibrating seat; the liability gap in traffic law; Tesla's projected 2016 autopilot car. org 4 (rung 5 fails: the capabilities paragraph and the law/liability paragraph could swap without loss, and the conclusion largely re-lists paragraph 2 and 3; rung 4 met, frame present, all parts on topic). dev 3 (patchwriting cap: the law paragraph - 'Most driving laws focus on keeping drivers, passengers, and pedrstrians safe... Automakers are continuing their work on the assumption that the problems ahead will be solved' - is source phrasing stitched in unmarked and untransformed, which caps the trait at 3 even though the ladder would otherwise reach rung 4). conv 3 (rung 4 fails: 'if something fails and someone is injures' and 'be we are getting closer' need repair, on top of an accumulation - windsheild, pedrstrians, asumption, acheived, postiton, truley). arg 4 (rung 5 fails on (d): the conclusion lands where the prompt's framing already puts it, and the liability question is raised but never folded back into the position; rung 4 met - the 'what if you fall asleep' objection is answered with why the notification systems address it).

Prompt (source-based): should facial-expression-reading technology be used in schools? Claim = it is useful and should be in schools. Support is entirely the writer's own projected uses, no source material: detecting a depressed student and alerting a counselor before suicidal thoughts develop; flagging a student struggling on a test so a teacher can help; detecting nervousness in a student with malevolent intent to reduce attack risk. org 3 (rung 4 fails: the second paragraph is a digression on students feeling watched that ends by saying kids may not care, contradicting rather than supporting the claim, and it starts one job and finishes another). dev 4 (rung 5 fails: nothing is specific throughout - every support is a conditional scenario, no named case or figure; rung 4 met, the mechanism from support to claim is stated - sense the emotion, alert the counselor, reach the child before the crisis). conv 2 (rung 3 fails: 'this may be a thing people might want to keep in schools for if people felt as though they were being watched by an electronic may keep them a bit on edge' and 'sensing there emotions of there action may be the one way' leave the reader guessing at the intended meaning, not merely repairing). arg 4 (rung 5 fails on (d): the conclusion is what the prompt's framing implies; rung 4 met - the fairness objection is raised and answered with a stated why: knowing support is available reduces stress rather than adding it).

Prompt: should driverless cars be developed? Claim is qualified from the outset - yes, but manufactured for the blind, elderly and those without full driving capability rather than for the average person. Support: very few people over 70 retain the driving ability and safety they had when younger; a computer at the wheel with sensors could recognise danger and take over from an intoxicated driver; the blind, wounded and deaf face transportation difficulties technology could remove. org 4 (rung 5 fails: elderly, drunk driving and handicapped are three interchangeable supports, each closed by a restating topic sentence; rung 4 met). dev 4 (rung 5 fails: the explanations restate the support - 'The driverless car would be a safe and effective transportation method for the elderly, this is one reason why driverless car should be manufactored'; rung 4 met, support is specific enough - over 70, sensors, blind/wounded/deaf - and the connection is stated). conv 4 (rung 5 fails: manufactored/maufactored recurs throughout, 'prevent from an accident' is wrong word choice, and the referent of 'Though they could take control of the wheel' is unclear; rung 4 otherwise holds, errors are visible but cost nothing). arg 5 (rung 5 met: the position is qualified where the issue warrants - explicitly not for the average driver - and the governing principle is made explicit in the conclusion, 'technology is not always meant for fun... when it can greatly improve the life of the eldery or handicapped, it should be developed'; rung 6 fails because the intro's boundary is never returned to and the drunk-driving reason quietly cuts across it).

Prompt (source-based): was the Face on Mars created by aliens or is it a natural landform? Claim = natural landform, held throughout. Support: the pictures were taken ten times for clear vision; when the image appeared on the JPL site people saw a natural landform; the writer's own explanation that a shadow at a bad camera angle can resemble a face. Much of the rest is circular - 'there aren't any aliens', 'never have I ever seen an alien', 'I have never heard of aliens creating the Face'. org 3 (rung 4 fails: two of the four body units repeat the opening without adding to it, and the opening paragraph carries several jobs at once - evidence, personal anecdote, and 'aliens are going to take over the world'). dev 3 (rung 4 fails: the specific source details - ten pictures, the JPL image - are listed with the reader left to connect them, and the load-bearing support restates the claim it is meant to support; rung 3 met on those source particulars). conv 3 (rung 4 fails: 'have I never of anyone capturing pictures' and 'I have never heard of aliens creating the Face, knowing aliens creating anything else' are word-omission slips needing repair on re-reading, plus 'a a shadow', exageratting; meaning stays recoverable so rung 3 holds). arg 4 (rung 5 fails: the opposing view is named but answered by assertion that aliens do not exist, and the conclusion circles back to the opening; rung 4 met - the shadow-and-camera-angle explanation gives a why for the resemblance rather than just denying it).

Prompt: argue to a state senator for keeping or abolishing the Electoral College. Claim = 'the Electoral College is important becase it is a process' - circular and never revisited. What follows is a run of near-verbatim source text: the founding-fathers compromise sentence, the three-stage process, 538 electors and 270 to win, and the 23rd Amendment passage retaining the source's own orienting phrase 'in the following discussion, the word state also refers to the District of Columbia', which makes no sense inside a letter. org 3 (rung 4 fails: no closing at all - the letter stops on a winner-take-all definition - and the body describes process rather than holding to the importance claim). dev 1 (the response is predominantly copied: after the opening sentence almost every clause is source phrasing, and once the descriptive process material is set aside as not bearing on the importance claim nothing assessable remains). conv 3 (rung 4 fails: the process sentences are fragments - 'The meeting of the electors where they vote for President and Vice President' - that need a re-read to be seen as a list, and misspellings accumulate: becase, Eletoral, comromise, qualificatied, mjority, elction, canidate; rung 3 holds, nothing must be guessed). arg 2 (rung 3 fails: the position is the prompt's term handed back with no commitment, 'important because it is a process' restates rather than reasons, and the letter abandons the stance for description).

Prompt (source-based): should driverless cars be developed? Claim = yes, stated in the first sentence with three announced reasons - half the fuel of today's taxis, more flexibility than a bus, easier and more enjoyable driving. Support: the car steers, accelerates and brakes itself and notifies the driver when the road requires human skill; in-car entertainment and information systems using heads-up displays that switch off when the driver must take over; half the fuel use of today's taxis. org 4 (rung 5 fails: the fuel paragraph and the 'easier for drivers' paragraph could swap freely, and the body reverses the intro's own order, confirming the supports are interchangeable; rung 4 met). dev 4 (rung 5 fails: the enjoyment paragraph is circular - a driverless car would be more enjoyable because the driver would enjoy relaxing - and the flexibility claim gets only 'more room, and do more things'; rung 4 met, connections are stated with a because, e.g. the displays turn off when the driver needs to take over). conv 4 (rung 5 fails: sentence shape is flat, nearly every sentence is a 'would' construction, so variety is absent; rung 4 holds - an driverless, accelertate, flexibity, 'the car notify' are visible but nothing needs repair). arg 4 (rung 5 fails: no opposing position is engaged, the qualification 'the driver would stil have to watch the road' is dropped rather than developed, and the conclusion re-lists the intro; rung 4 met, the safety of heads-up displays and the fuel saving are each given a stated why).

Prompt (source-based): write to persuade others to join the Seagoing Cowboys program. Claim = you should join, stated in the opening and repeated in the close. Support: the writer was hired to care for horses, young cows and mules shipped overseas; nine trips, the most of any seagoing cowboy; travel to Europe, China, Greece and Italy on cattle boats; time left over to relax. org 3 (rung 4 fails: the frame is perfunctory - the close stops and then restarts with fresh appeals - and the body is a single unit that begins as personal history and ends as a recruiting pitch, fusing jobs mid-sentence). dev 4 (rung 5 fails: the countries, the record and the cattle boats are listed with no explanation and the elaboration is restatement - 'it changed my whole live and this can be you too'; rung 4 met, the essay states the connection at least once, 'If you love animals you will love this job as much as I do'). conv 3 (rung 4 fails: run-ons need repair on re-reading - 'I might as will give it a try i thought so I did and once I got into this it changed my whole live and this can be you too' and 'you should join you will have a lot of fun in this program Its also will open the world to you' - with im, didnt, oversea, live for life; rung 3 holds, meaning is always recoverable). arg 3 (rung 4 fails: every benefit is asserted rather than reasoned - travel, the record and the free time are stated as appealing with no why given - and the same appeal is recirculated in the conclusion; the animals line functions as a stated connection for Development but supplies no principle linking the job to the reader's reason to join).
